# Go Decisions

What gofmt decides, so a reviewer does not.

## Format

One tool decides the layout of a file, so a reviewer does not.

| id | title | check | fix | requirement |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [`go/formatted`](#a-go-file-is-as-gofmt-writes-it) | A Go file is as gofmt writes it | error · command | safe |  |

### A Go file is as gofmt writes it

`go/formatted` · file · error · command · fix: safe

*Vertical and horizontal openness, indentation and the placement of braces are team rules, and a team keeps them by letting one tool decide, not by reviewing them (Martin, Clean Code ch. 5 Team rules). The check is the tool's own list mode: one finding per file it would change, at line 1, that names the file. The fix is the tool as a filter, which writes the file as it formats it; it has the lowest priority, so the fix of any other decision wins an overlap and the formatting follows it as a safe follow-up of the change. The programs are the bundled catalog's own, so they run in a project nobody trusted.*

A Go file MUST equal the output of gofmt.

Derived from: Martin, Clean Code (2008), G24 Follow Standard Conventions; Martin, Clean Code (2008), ch. 5 Vertical openness and density; Martin, Clean Code (2008), ch. 5 Horizontal openness and indentation; Martin, Clean Code (2008), ch. 5 Team rules; gofmt: https://pkg.go.dev/cmd/gofmt

--- a/example.go
+++ b/example.go
@@ -1,3 +1,3 @@
